title: Cognify: Supercharging Gen-AI Workflows With Hierarchical Autotuning

problem.claim: Gen-AI workflows involving multiple model calls, tool or API calls, data retrieval, or generic code execution are often tuned manually in an ad-hoc way, which is time-consuming and error-prone.

gap.claim: The unique properties of gen-AI workflows require new optimization techniques beyond changes to workflow structure, operators, and prompts.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes AdaSeek, an adaptive hierarchical search algorithm for autotuning gen-AI workflows.
AdaSeek organizes tuning methods into layers according to the user-specified total search budget and allocates budget across layers based on layer complexity.
The authors implement AdaSeek in a workflow autotuning framework called Cognify.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Cognify improves generation quality by up to 2.8× across the evaluated workflows.
Cognify reduces execution monetary cost by up to 10× across the evaluated workflows.
Cognify reduces end-to-end latency by 2.7× across the evaluated workflows.

narrative_sequence.summary: Gen-AI workflow tuning is commonly manual, ad hoc, time-consuming, and error-prone.
The paper proposes systematic automatic tuning and identifies workflow structure, operator, and prompt changes as relevant tuning dimensions.
AdaSeek performs adaptive hierarchical search, allocating and redistributing search budget across tuning layers and configurations using complexity and workflow-level evaluation results.
Cognify is evaluated on six types of workflows, including RAG-based question answering and text-to-SQL transformation.
The authors report improvements in generation quality, monetary cost, and end-to-end latency.

source_observation.claim: Search budget is distributed across hierarchical tuning layers according to layer complexity and later redistributed using workflow-level evaluation results.

interpretation.claim: Hierarchical budget allocation can focus optimization effort on more promising configurations while limiting effort spent on less useful ones.

application.claim: For complex gen-AI workflows, autotuning systems could allocate and reallocate a fixed search budget across tuning dimensions rather than optimize all configurations uniformly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy is effective outside the evaluated workflow types or under different search budgets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six workflow types beyond RAG-based QA and text-to-SQL transformation.
The abstract does not describe baselines, evaluation metrics, experimental conditions, or the basis of the reported multipliers.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or reproducibility information.
